ArtifactCheck.description:
A check of the published package file itself, made by hand, not by a box.

Box limits cannot change what a published file holds, so this, or a person's run, is the
only ground for a failed verdict. The pipeline never writes one.

artifact.description: The published file checked, e.g. a wheel on PyPI.

finding.description: What the file holds, or lacks.

ArtifactCheck.title: ArtifactCheck

Check.description: A command that shows the install works, and the text it should print.
Check.title: Check

DocsRubric.description: The model's rubric answer behind install_docs, kept so scores can be refreshed without a call.

sources_sha.description: sha256 of the rendered sources the model read.

unquoted.description: Items set to 0 because their quote is not in the sources.

DocsRubric.title: DocsRubric

DocsRubricItems.description: The eight documentation items of B.3's install_docs component, graded from the sources only.

config_and_keys.description: Configuration, environment variables and API keys, or that none are needed.

first_run_example.description: A first command or example to run after install, with the output to expect.

install_per_os.description: Copy-paste install commands for each platform it supports.

license_and_platforms.description: The license and the platforms it runs on, as the sources name them.

prerequisites.description: What must exist first (runtimes, OS packages, hardware, accounts), or that nothing does.

troubleshooting_uninstall.description: Common problems or an FAQ, and how to update or uninstall.

what_it_does.description: What the software does and its main features.

who_it_is_for.description: Who it is for, or the jobs it suits.

DocsRubricItems.title: DocsRubricItems

score.description: 0-2, the two samples' mean; null with any other status.

comfortable.description: Readable, a clear main area, nothing broken or covering the work.

findable.description: The controls each operation needed were visible, labelled, expected.

ready.description: Ready to use on opening (first look; starts from the screen judge).

responsive.description: The result showed on the screen, or an error said what to do.

EaseFinding.description:
One problem the reviewer saw, with the text on its own screenshot it cites: found by pickfit's OCR or in the
page's DOM, or (comfort.v1's visual defects, which are kept either way) unverified.

box.description: [x_min, y_min, x_max, y_max], 0-1000 over the screenshot.

cause.description: Only app problems lower a score; the operator's and the sandbox's are listed, never scored.

kind.description: comfort.v1: the kind of measurable visual defect.

operation.description: The operation it happened in (in-use findings).

quote.description: The text on the screen it cites.

screenshot.description: The screenshot's file name in the run's evidence folder.

severity.description: comfort.v1: major hides, garbles or makes hard to read content a user needs; minor does not.

EaseFinding.title: EaseFinding

FeatureCheck.description:
Whether a run exercised one of the tool's advertised features, and with which smoke tests.

checked: a smoke test it cites passed (the run's smoke tests are the fresh-box replay's).
not_checked: nothing exercised it here; reason says why. test_failed: its test ran and failed
while the tool otherwise worked; failure says whether only this box explains it (sandbox) or
the tool's own error does (tool: suspected, as a user would hit it, never a failed verdict).

failure.description: test_failed only. sandbox: only this box explains it (no GPU, network, display, service); tool: the tool's own error, which a user following the README would hit too.

reason.description: not_checked: why not; test_failed with failure sandbox: the box's limit, if known.

smoke_tests.description: Indexes into the run's smoke_tests that exercise it.

FeatureCheck.title: FeatureCheck

FeatureGuide.description: One advertised feature as a person reads it: a plain title, and for a feature a run checked, how to use it.

feature.description: The feature exactly as in features.

steps.description: How to use it, from what the run did; only for a feature run_id checked, else empty.

title.description: The feature in plain words, sentence case.

FeatureGuide.title: FeatureGuide

FieldEvidence.description: Where one field's value came from.

quote.description: Verbatim quote; null for API values and sandbox results.

FieldEvidence.title: FieldEvidence

GuiCheck.description:
How far a GUI app got on the box's virtual display (Linux, Xvfb, no window manager).

Recorded only for a launch whose checked screenshot the judge read. window: a mapped window whose X
client is one of the app's processes (per the X server), showing something other than the app's UI
(`screen`: a sign-in wall, a crash, a blank or loading screen); ui_rendered: the judge saw the app's own
interface in a crop of its windows (its main screen or its first-run screen); action_checked: also, an
operation (`operations`) passed pickfit's own check in the replay and the feature judge saw it show a
listed feature working. A launch supports install; action_checked supports function.

display.description: e.g. Xvfb 1280x800x24, no window manager, no GPU.

operations.description: Goals pickfit operated the app toward, and what its checks found.

screen.description: What the screen judge saw in the crop of the app's windows.

window_title.description: Set by the app; data only.

GuiCheck.title: GuiCheck

GuiOperation.description:
One goal pickfit reached through the app's own UI (gui_operate.py), in the fresh box's replay.

Muse Spark Open chose each click, text and key from pickfit's screenshots; pickfit performed them as
the display user (the app never acts for itself), then checked the result itself: a file the app wrote,
read by root; the clipboard, read by the display user; text the screen judge read on pickfit's last
screenshot; or a file root read before the app started and found gone after it stopped. The goal and the
expected text hold {nonce} where pickfit put a fresh word.

format.description: file: the format it had to have.

goal.description: What the operator was asked to do.

observed.description: pickfit's line about what the check found.

passed.description: pickfit's check, never the operator's word.

replay.description: actions: the recorded actions passed again; operated: the operator ran the goal again.

smoke_test.description: Index into the run's smoke_tests: this operation's check.

target.description: file: the file, or the folder searched; gone: the file deleted.

GuiOperation.title: GuiOperation

InstallGuide.description:
Install steps for one OS, as get_install_guide returns them.

basis says where the steps come from: replayed (passed a fresh-sandbox
replay), human (done by hand on a real machine), or readme_claim (written
in the README, never run; must not be presented as verified).

manual_steps.description: Steps only the user can do, e.g. grant a permission.

InstallGuide.title: InstallGuide

Judge.description: Separate model call that reads the screenshot and log.
Judge.title: Judge

McpHandshake.description:
What pickfit's MCP probe saw when a fresh box started the server (the replay's check).

Names come from the server and are untrusted: the probe keeps only safe characters, and
tool descriptions never leave the box (only the probe's own pattern flags do).

called_tool.description: A tool tools/call ran without an error (level service).

launch.description: argv that started the server, as the replay ran it: the probe's own over stdio, the background setup's over HTTP.

offline.description: true: the handshake passed with the network off; false: only with it on.

tool_count.description: Tools listed, also those past MCP_TOOLS_MAX.

url.description: streamable_http: the local URL the probe posted to.

McpHandshake.title: McpHandshake

McpServer.description:
How an AI client uses this MCP server, as the sources claim it (README, not run).

What a box actually saw lives in verification.runs[].mcp; the index prefers that.
McpServer.title: McpServer

Outcomes.description: Usage outcomes synced from D1, by reporter. Only external reports count in scores.

replaced_by.description: External reports: replacement slug or name -> count.

Outcomes.title: Outcomes

Pitfall.description: A difference between the README and what actually worked.

kind.description: readme_wrong: a user following the README would hit it; sandbox: only the box needed it; tool_handled: the tool did the step by itself; note: worth knowing, nothing to fix. null: not tagged (older runs).

Pitfall.title: Pitfall

age_days.description: Repo age; velocity applies from 90 days.

packages.description: Registry packages that link back to the repo, e.g. 'npm:adapty'.

PopularitySignals.description: The seven popularity signals of B.3; null when not collected.
PopularitySignals.title: PopularitySignals

cap.description: QUALITY_CAPS[cap_reason]; the lowest cap that applies.

confidence.description: Share of weight that had data.

visual.description: Formulas ending +visual.v1: the visual check's factor, the total before it, its app defects.

score.description: 0-1; null when data is missing (dropped from the denominator).

QualityComponents.description:
The six quality components of B.3 (nominal weights 35/20/15/10/10/10+).

A hosted web app (formula web.v1, pickfit/score.py) adds browser_facts and gives the four components a
README and a repository feed weight 0: it is opened, not installed. Other records never carry it.

browser_facts.description: Web apps only: what the browser run saw (account, data sent, ads, offline).

usability.description: Formulas gui.v1 and web.v2 only: the record's usability score / 100 (pickfit/usability.py).

usage_outcomes.description: Only external reports count. <3 reports: weight 10, score null (dropped from the denominator); 3-9: 10; 10-29: 20; >=30: 30 (usage_outcomes_weight).

QualityComponents.title: QualityComponents

Release.description: Latest release from the host API.
Release.title: Release

Repo.description: Repository facts from the host API.

full_name.description: owner/name as the host reports it now.

Repo.title: Repo

quote.description: For 1 or 2: a snippet (<=200 chars) copied verbatim from one source that shows the item; null for 0.

score.description: 0: missing; 1: partial or vague; 2: clear and complete.

RunEvidence.description: Where to see the proof. Screenshots are redrawn from terminal output.

evidence_url.description: Public run page or trace JSON (MCP evidence_url).

RunEvidence.title: RunEvidence

RunVideo.description:
A short captioned clip of pickfit operating a GUI or web app to check its features (pickfit/verify/video.py).

A fresh box replayed this run's steps and operations (a web app: a second, recorded visit replaying the first
visit's actions without a model) while pickfit recorded its own screen; Muse Spark Open
watched each recording with pickfit's action log and picked whole segments, kept in their order (a speed-up
is labelled on screen), and then watched the cut and confirmed that each caption shows on screen. Captions
claim only checks that passed in this run and again in the recorded replay. The clip's first frame says it
was recorded by pickfit in a sandbox, and on what date; it names each raw recording and its sha256.

chapters.description: The clip's chapters in time order, covering it whole: the first card at 0, one chapter for each run of segments of one feature, the last card.

features.description: The run's checked features the clip shows.

model.description: Who picked the segments and checked the captions.

recording_run.description: The recorded replay of this run's steps (its evidence id).

RunVideo.title: RunVideo

docs_rubric.description: Rubric behind quality.components.install_docs; null when not graded.

SecurityCheck.description:
Known vulnerabilities in what a fresh install brings (sec.v1, pickfit/security.py; 念誠 11/3).

No model call: the dependencies are resolved the way a person installing it today gets them (a published package
through npm --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts or uv pip compile --no-build, neither runs package code; else the
repository's lockfiles, Python re-resolved from pyproject.toml since pip and uv do not read uv.lock), without
development dependencies and without lockfiles of parts the person does not install (docs sites, editor extensions,
CI actions). Every resolved version is looked up on OSV.dev; any high or critical advisory, fixed or not, counts.

advisories_total.description: Distinct vulnerabilities among the findings: one advisory (with its aliases) on several packages or versions counts once. Absent on a check written before 11/3 evening.

findings_total.description: Every finding (one per advisory on each package version), though findings keeps at most 60.

sources.description: What was resolved, e.g. 'npm:x@1.2.0' or a lockfile path.

SecurityCheck.title: SecurityCheck

SecurityFinding.description: One high or critical OSV advisory (or a malicious-package report) on a package a fresh install brings.

advisory.description: OSV id, e.g. GHSA-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx or MAL-2025-1.

fixed_in.description: The lowest fixed version above the installed one; null when none is out.

SecurityFinding.title: SecurityFinding

SetupStep.description: A command a smoke test needs first: an input file, a server to query.

background.description: Started detached and left running (a server).

SetupStep.title: SetupStep

offline.description: true: passed with the network off; false: passed only with it on (needs the network); null: not run offline.

setup.description: Run first, in order, with the network on.

is_treasure.description: Tool, verified, not archived, quality >= 80 and popularity <= 45.

value.description: T = quality * (1 - popularity/100); null when either is null.

Usability.description:
How easy a GUI or web app was to use when pickfit's AI operator used it in a sandbox (ease.v1).

Muse Spark 1.3 read the screenshots and action log of one passed run against a fixed checklist, twice; every
score cites text pickfit found on its own screenshot. Under comfort.v1 (prompt_version ending "+comfort.v1"),
comfortable comes instead from Muse Wonder listing measurable visual defects in one call. It is pickfit's AI
operator in a sandbox, not users' opinion. Not checked: screen readers, keyboard-only use, phones.

basis.description: operated: an operation passed pickfit's check; first_look: only the first screens were seen.

inputs_sha.description: sha256 over the prompts' text and every image's.

run_id.description: The run whose screenshots and log were read; stale once that run is gone.

sandbox.description: The display or browser, as the run recorded it.

score.description: 0-100; null for a first look alone.

verdict.description: >=70 easy, 40-69 some friction, <40 hard; none for a first look.

Usability.title: Usability

UsageGuide.description:
Reader-facing text written by a model from the record and the run behind its checked features
(pickfit/usage_guide.py). It adds words, never claims: a feature gets steps only when run_id checked it.

model.description: The model that wrote this text.

open_hint.description: How to start it once installed, in plain words (GUI apps: where it appears).

run_id.description: The passed run the steps rest on; null when no run checked a feature.

UsageGuide.title: UsageGuide

Verification.description:
Summary over runs; keeps only the latest run per OS, arch and method.

Older runs live in git history. Write-back never replaces a passed run with one
that did not pass, and writes a failure only on an OS with no passed run.

checked_at.description: Latest run time; null when no runs.

Verification.title: Verification

VerificationRun.description: One verification attempt on one OS (C.3).

artifact_check.description: A check of the published package by hand: the only ground for a failed sandbox run.

features.description: Which advertised features this run exercised. Empty: none recorded (the tool lists none, or it was verified before pickfit checked features).

gpu.description: The GPU the box had, as its driver named it (e.g. Tesla T4); none: the box had no GPU.

gui.description: A GUI app's launch on a virtual display: the strongest evidence tier it reached.

mcp.description: MCP servers: the handshake a fresh box completed; required for a passed run of one.

microphone.description: The box's microphone: a simulated one that played words pickfit spoke for each check; none: the box had no audio input.

replayed.description: A fresh sandbox replayed the steps with the same outcome: for a passed run, the steps and checks passed again.

video.description: GUI and web apps: a captioned clip of pickfit operating the app to check its features.

web.description: Hosted web apps: what the sandboxed browser saw; required for a passed run of one.

VerificationRun.title: VerificationRun

VideoChapter.description: A chapter of a clip, for the player's progress bar: the first card, each feature's segments, the last card.

feature.description: The video.features entry the chapter shows; null for the first and last cards.

start_s.description: Where the chapter starts in the clip, seconds.

VideoChapter.title: VideoChapter

VideoRaw.description:
One unedited screen recording a clip was cut from: one operation, from just before the app started until
pickfit's check had looked at the screen (pickfit/verify/record.py).

smoke_test.description: The operation's check: an index into the run's smoke_tests.

VideoRaw.title: VideoRaw

VisualCheck.description:
Measurable visual defects on the first screens of one passed GUI or web run (comfort.v1, pickfit/usability.py).

Muse Wonder looked at pickfit's own screenshots (the app right after start and at the end of its last passed
operation) and listed what a second person would find in the same spot: text cut off, overlaps, clipped controls,
bad wraps, low contrast, tiny text, raw markup, broken images, misalignment, cramping. Never taste, welcome
dialogs or what the sandbox causes. score: no app defect 2, minor ones only 1, any major 0.

inputs_sha.description: sha256 over the prompt and every image's sha256.

run_id.description: The run whose screenshots were read; stale once that run is gone.

score.description: Null when the sandbox broke the screen or no answer came.

VisualCheck.title: VisualCheck

VisualDeduction.description: What the visual check did to the total (formulas ending +visual.v1, pickfit/score.py apply_visual).

before.description: The formula's total before the factor.

factor.description: 1.0 for a clean check; 0.95 when it found an app-caused defect.

VisualDeduction.title: VisualDeduction

WebApp.description: A hosted web app (kind web_app): where to open it. What a browser saw lives in verification.runs[].web.

url.description: The address users open, as the sources give it.

WebApp.title: WebApp

WebCheck.description:
What pickfit saw of a hosted web app (kind web_app) in a sandboxed browser.

One session per site, no replay: sites are real and each is visited once, slowly. install: the URL loaded
to the app's own main screen (not an error page, a parked domain or a sign-in wall); function: also an
operation passed pickfit's own check. The other facts are what the browser's own records showed.

account_needed.description: An account or sign-in is needed for the core use; null when pickfit could not tell.

ads_seen.description: Ads on the page during the session; null when not looked at.

data_sent.description: none: pickfit typed data in or chose a file during an operation and no request carried it off the device; observed: a request did; unknown: not checked, or the requests could not tell.

data_sent_note.description: pickfit's line on what it saw.

final_url.description: Where it ended after redirects, when different.

offline.description: verified: a PWA reloaded with the network off and still worked; only PWAs are tested.

operations.description: Goals pickfit operated the site toward, and what its checks found.

pwa.description: Has a web app manifest and a service worker; null when not looked at.

screen.description: What the page showed once loaded.

third_party_domains.description: Distinct domains other than the site's own that the page contacted; null when not counted.

third_party_hosts.description: Those hosts, as the browser saw them (at most 50).

WebCheck.title: WebCheck

WebOperation.description:
One goal pickfit reached on a hosted web app through the page itself, in the run's one browser session.

Muse Spark chose each action from the page (browser-use); pickfit checked the result itself: text on the
page, an element, the URL, a downloaded file, the clipboard. Only side-effect-free operations (search,
in-page tools, games): no form that posts, mails, signs up or orders. The goal and the expected text hold
{nonce} where pickfit put a fresh word.

goal.description: What the operator was asked to do.

observed.description: pickfit's line about what the check found.

passed.description: pickfit's check, never the operator's word.

smoke_test.description: Index into the run's smoke_tests: this operation's check.

WebOperation.title: WebOperation

description: One software entry: the canonical file data/software/<slug>.json (software.v1).

features.description: The main features the sources advertise (quotes in evidence); verification.runs[].features says which a run exercised.

license.description: SPDX id from the host API; null when unknown or NOASSERTION.

mcp.description: Only for category mcp_server: transport, launch command, client config, env vars, tools.

platforms.description: Platforms the sources claim; tested results live in install and verification.

repo.description: Null only for a hosted web app with no public repository ('web:' id).

repo_id.description: Primary key: 'gh:' + GitHub numeric repository id; 'web:' + host and path for a web app with no repo.

security.description: Known high or critical vulnerabilities in what a fresh install brings (OSV.dev); null: not run yet.

slug.description: Never changes; also the file name. Renames go to aliases.

usability.description: Only for kind desktop_app and web_app: how easy pickfit's AI operator found it (ease.v1).

usage_guide.description: Plain feature titles and how-to steps for the tool page; generated text, see usage_guide.model.

visual_check.description: Only for kind desktop_app and web_app: measurable visual defects on pickfit's own screenshots.

web.description: Only for kind web_app: the URL to open.
